questions.q: How do you assign a value to a variable in Python?
options: With a single equals sign, e.g. customer_name = "Alex Rivera"
With a double equals sign, e.g. customer_name == "Alex Rivera"
Variables must be declared in a separate file before use
By declaring the type first, e.g. str customer_name = "Alex Rivera"
questions.explain: Python assignment uses a single equals sign, with no type declaration needed — Python figures out the type automatically from the value.

questions.q: What are the three basic data types covered in this lesson?
options: String (str), integer (int), and float
Text, number, and date
List, dictionary, and tuple
Integer, character, and boolean only
questions.explain: String for text, integer for whole numbers, and float for numbers with a decimal point cover almost everything used in this course.

questions.q: What does Python do with a comment (text after a #)?
options: Ignores it completely when running the code — it exists only for the human reading the code
Treats it as a variable name
Prints it to the output automatically
Executes it as if it were regular code
questions.explain: Comments are skipped entirely at runtime. They're documentation for whoever reads the code later, not instructions Python acts on.

questions.q: What is an f-string, and what is it used for?
options: A function that formats dates only
A special type of float number
A string prefixed with 'f' that lets you embed variables directly inside curly braces, for combining text and values in print statements
A way to declare a variable as read-only
questions.explain: An f-string like f"Total for {customer_name} is {order_total}" embeds variable values directly into a string — the cleaner, more common way to combine text and data in output.

questions.q: Is order_total the same variable as Order_Total in Python?
options: It depends on whether they're strings or numbers
No — Python variable names are case-sensitive, so these are two different variables
Yes, Python treats variable names as case-insensitive
Only if both are assigned the same value
questions.explain: Python is case-sensitive throughout, including variable names — order_total and Order_Total point to two completely separate values.
